name: httpserver
description: Serve SQL queries over HTTP from a running DuckDB process. Start a local endpoint, authenticate requests, and return query results as JSON.

cta.title: DuckDB as a small HTTP query API
cta.description: Install httpserver to put a SQL endpoint in front of a DuckDB instance — single-key or Basic auth, embedded UI, no extra infrastructure.

quickStart.title: Start a local SQL endpoint
quickStart.description: Run the SQL in an interactive DuckDB session, keep it open, and send the curl request from a second terminal.
quickStart.sql:
-- Demo credentials: change these before using your own data.
SELECT httpserve_start('127.0.0.1', 9999, 'demo:change-me');

-- In another terminal:
-- curl --user 'demo:change-me' --data 'SELECT 42 AS answer' \
--   http://127.0.0.1:9999/

-- After trying the request, stop the server with:
-- SELECT httpserve_stop();
quickStart.note: The endpoint executes SQL in this DuckDB process. The loopback address keeps this example local. See the read-only database recipe before serving data to other clients.
quickStart.requirements: Use a native DuckDB session and a free local port 9999. The process must remain running while you make the HTTP request.

introduction.title: Let an HTTP client query a running DuckDB database
paragraphs: HTTP Server starts a listener inside DuckDB. Clients submit SQL over HTTP and receive JSON results, giving scripts or an internal application access to an existing DuckDB session without a database client library.

The serving process must remain running. Choose which database and connection state it exposes, and configure authentication before giving other clients access. A read-only database is useful when the endpoint should serve queries without accepting changes.
